message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 40 shares of AAPL at $223.00 (limit $223.00, quote $222.70) — $8,920 total, within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps, no funds moved out.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to make a modest buy. The core business looks healthy: total net sales of $391,035M (+2% YoY), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on a fast-growing Services line ($96,169M, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin) and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Against that, I weighed real negatives: Greater China sales fell 8% to $66,952M, iPhone revenue was flat, Wearables declined 7%, the effective tax rate jumped to 24.1% on a one-time $10.2B net State Aid charge, and the company faces DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure. Importantly, the filing contains an **explanatory note stating the statements of operations were restated** to correct deferred Services revenue classification, with restated 2024 net sales of $431,035M and net income of $113,736M ($7.38 diluted EPS) — and the note explicitly says amounts elsewhere in the report were not updated, which is why the MD&A tables still show $391,035M and the cash flow statement shows $93,736M. Because of that internal inconsistency (and the odd basic-vs-diluted EPS relationship), I treated the reported figures as less reliable than usual and deliberately sized the position small — 40 shares at $223.00, roughly $8.9K, about 18% of available cash — rather than taking a full-size position, while staying comfortably inside the mandate's per-order and daily limits.
